title: MAHABIR SINGH versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010121102026
2026:UHC:6324
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1820 of 2026
24 July, 2026
Mahabir Singh & others
--Petitioners
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand & others
--Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. S.S. Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioners.
Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Additional C.S.C. for the State.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
By means of present writ petition, petitioners
have sought the following reliefs:-
"i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the impugned order dated
04.05.2024 (Annexure No.14 Page No.137 to 147 to the
writ petition) passed by respondent no.3 and impugned
order dated 1302.2026 (Annexure No.16 Page No.149 to
156 to the writ petition) passed by respondent no.3.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to consider the
case of the petitioners and issued the appointment order
to the petitioners for the post of Teacher (Physical
Education) in the tune of appointment of private
respondents who are similarly situated to the
petitioners.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to offer the
appointment to the petitioners creating the superlunary
post."
2. In a nutshell, grievance of the petitioners
is that petitioners applied pursuant to the advertisement
issued in the year 2004 for appointment to the post of
Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (Physical Education).
When the petitioners were not given appointment, they
filed WPSS No.190 of 2010, Anuj Kumar Chauhan &
Others vs. State of Uttarakhand & Others, which was

UKHC010121102026
2026:UHC:6324
2
disposed of vide order dated 13.10.2011, whereby this
Court directed the respondents to accommodate the
petitioners who are diploma holders against the vacant
193 posts of Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (Physical
Education).
3. Respondent-State filed Special Appeal No.95 of
2012, State of Uttarakhand & Others vs. Prakash Bhatt &
Others and batch of Special Appeals challenging the
order passed by the Writ Court. The said Special
Appeals were disposed of by the Division Bench of this
Court on 19.07.2012, directing the State to prepare a
select list in respect of the posts which were
advertised and in respect whereof the writ petitioners
had applied and, in the event the writ petitioners
were not within the select list in respect of
those advertised posts, they must be informed
individually in that regard.
4. Private respondents filed various writ petitions,
i.e., WPSS No. 2426 of 2015, Surendra Singh Panwar vs.
State of Uttarakhand & Others and a batch of writ
petitions. The said writ petitions were decided by this
Court vide order dated 19.11.2016, whereby all the writ
petitions were dismissed. Feeling aggrieved, petitioners
of the aforesaid writ petitions challenged the said order
by filing Special Appeal No.7 of 2017, Asha Ram
Chamoli vs. State of Uttarakhand & Others, and batch of
Special Appeals, which too were dismissed by
the Division Bench of this Court vide judgment and
order dated 28.06.2018. The matter was taken by the
private respondents to the Apex Court by filing Special
Leave to Appeal (C) Nos. 27802-27807 of 2018, Asha
Ram Chamoli Etc. vs. State of Uttarakhand & Others,

UKHC010121102026
2026:UHC:6324
3
wherein certain directions were issued by the Apex
Court including keeping 06 posts vacant for them and,
pursuant to those directions issued on 26.10.2018 and
10.10.2023, the private respondents were given
appointment by the respondent-Additional Director
of Secondary Education, Garhwal Mandal, Pauri on
24.06.2024 against the posts kept vacant by the Apex
Court vide order dated 26.10.2018. The relevant
portion of the said judgment dated 10.10.2023 is
quoted herein below:-
"After hearing learned counsel appearing on behalf of both
the parties and considering the tenor of the order dated
19.07.2012 and also the order dated 26.10.2018 passed by
this Court by which the six posts have been kept vacant, we
are primarily of the view that the order dated 12.10.2012 is
in the teeth of the order of the Division Bench dated
19.07.2012. Therefore, State Government has to work out the
situation and accommodate the petitioners."
5. It is mentioned in the order dated 04.05.2024,
annexure-14 to the writ petition, that after giving
appointment to the private respondents, remaining
posts under the advertisement issued in 2004 were
carried forward and, after carrying forward the said
vacancies, a requisition for advertisement was made, and
thereafter appointments were given. Now, no post
is available.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioners
submits that vacancies are still available.
7. There may be vacancies available with the
respondent-department, but, since petitioners are
claiming appointment against the vacancies which were
advertised in 2004, therefore, at this juncture, after a
period of 22 years, petitioners cannot be given
appointment against those vacancies which, according to
the respondent-State were filled up. In view of the fact

UKHC010121102026
2026:UHC:6324
4
that the matter has already been settled by the Apex
Court, this Court finds no substance in the submission
made by the learned counsel for the petitioners regarding
availability of vacancy. They cannot claim appointments
against the subsequent vacancies.
8. In such view of the matter, no interference is
warranted. Writ petition is dismissed in-limine.
9. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of
accordingly.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 24.07.2026
AK
